items.title: Neighborhood exhibition plan
items.summary: A planning note for a small exhibition about everyday places, with an open curatorial choice between themes and chronology.
items.content:
# I01 · Neighborhood exhibition plan

Fictional practice material. Date: 2026-03-10. Author: City Memory project team (invented).

We are planning a small exhibition about how residents remember everyday places. The starting materials include an interview excerpt, a photograph label and a register of printed ephemera. Visitors should be able to move from a theme to the original material.

We have not chosen whether to organize the exhibition by theme or by date. Chronology may be difficult where dates are approximate or unknown. “Public memory” and “Exhibitions” are useful starting themes; they can be revised.

items.title: Remembering Canal Park
items.summary: A fictional speaker remembers Canal Park through the route used to reach it. The interview date is unknown.
items.content:
I02 · Remembering Canal Park

Fictional practice material. Interview date: unknown. Speaker: Mira (invented).

Mira: I remember Canal Park by the route we took, not the year. We passed the bakery and then the footbridge. When the bridge closed, the park felt farther away even though it had not moved.

Researcher's note: This excerpt can help us ask how a route shapes the memory of a place. It does not establish the year of the closure. Keep the speaker's memory distinct from the researcher's interpretation.

items.title: Market Square photograph label
items.summary: A tentative label for a photograph of Market Square. Its date and the identification of one building remain uncertain.
items.content:
# I03 · Market Square photograph label

Fictional practice material. Date label: c. 1975. Photographer: unknown.

The supplied label describes a photograph of Market Square with a temporary stage. One building is tentatively identified as the former bakery. Neither the date nor that identification has been verified.

No image is included in this practice folder. Treat this as a label to organize, not as an image you have examined. Preserve “c. 1975” and the tentative identification.

items.title: Reading the exhibition materials
items.summary: An interpretive note comparing an interview, a photograph label and a poster register. It proposes questions rather than settling the chronology.
items.content:
# I04 · Reading the exhibition materials

Fictional practice material. Date: 2026-03-12. Author: project researcher (invented).

I02 organizes memory through a route, while I03's label tries to locate a scene in time. I05's poster register adds another kind of public account: how an event was announced. These can be grouped for comparison, but the grouping is my interpretation.

Could the exhibition compare remembered routes, labeled scenes and public announcements? Do not turn that question into a conclusion that all three describe the same event. The sources do not establish that connection.
